newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Reuters still keen to return cash.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Reuters still keen to return cash.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc chief executive Peter Job said on Tuesday the company remained keen to return surplus cash to shareholders and did not want to be pressed into acquisitions.
"We would like to return excess cash to shareholders," he said in an interview. "We don't want to be pressed just because we have money to make acquisitions we don't really want," he said.
Job said he hoped other companies might now try to find a way to return cash to shareholders after the company's own plan to do so was "stamped on" by the UK government last year.
Asked about possible acquisitions, Job said, "Big acquisitions? Well, we don't really want to go outside our field of activity."

He noted that competition was keen in the areas where Reuters was active. "The competitors themselves are not that numerous, so if you went out and bought a big competitor, all you do is reduce your clients' choice."
Job said he could not comment on reports linking Reuters with Dow Jones and Co Inc but noted they had been roundly denied by the other party.

Asked about the recent falls in the Reuters share price, Job said, "It does seem to me that the markets have a lot of sense behind them. Foreign exchange is a problem...If the pound continues very strong, it does reduce our rate of growth considerably, as we are saying."
But he added this did not affect the fundamentals of the company very much.
Reuters shares were down 22-1/2p at 619-1/2p by 1211 GMT in heavy trade of over 15 million shares.
The current share price compares with a high of over eight pounds reached last October.

Job said that earlier suggestions that sales of the new 3000 series of products had been disappointing were a "feature of the quiet period", referring to the time when companies may not comment on their business performance before releasing results.

"Sales are going really rather well." He said the current level of sales of about 14,700 was perhaps rather more than Reuters had expected at this point. He said the company was "shooting for" 30,000 sales this year.
